segments.line: A week later, Ellie gets sick.
A cut on her knee from the street.
Then a fever.
Then red lines creeping up her leg.
The doctor comes. He's kind, and he's honest. There's nothing he can give her.
Mo's mom sits by the bed all night with a wet cloth.
Mo tries to make Ellie laugh.
She asks for the star. You turn on the flashlight, and she smiles.
Somehow, that's worse.
Antibiotics don't exist yet. Penicillin won't be discovered until September 1928, almost two years from now. That's real.
You know exactly what penicillin is.
You even have a photo of a pharmacy shelf full of it.
But a photo can't cure anyone. You need someone who can make it.
That night, the man in the grey suit comes back. He doesn't bring money this time. He brings a laboratory. Chemists. Equipment.
'Give us the phone, ' he says, 'and we'll make your medicine. Whatever you can show us. '
Mo is sitting on the stairs. He heard everything.
Ellie is asleep upstairs, burning hot.
Give it away, and the future changes. Maybe millions of people you'll never meet live, or don't. Keep it, and a little girl might never see 1927.
You think about every time travel movie you've ever seen. Don't change anything. Don't touch anything.
Easy to say, when it's not your family.
You look down at the screen. Nine percent.
